title: what the plugin says about itself is true
description: Tasks: (1) SECURITY.md names the five open secret-read shapes listed as Known open in 2.3.0 at class level, and corrects the post-detection sentence about commands 'provably unable to write'; the documented-gap rows become a characterization test in the repo. (2) Fix false claims: usage --backfill 'writes nothing', status.md's nonexistent /audit:run-gate, examples/README 'never dirties the tree', tests/_harness.py 'macos in CI', the fsync docstring in _manifest_io. (3) QUICKSTART is the only quick-start; other docs link to it; the README's first screen states who it is for and who does not need it. (4) Re-record the demo GIF and give it a text digest in captured-at.json so its words cannot rot unseen. (5) CONTRIBUTING gets a one-page 'Your first change'; add issue and PR templates. (6) Decision record: optional modules (panel, usage views, ADO, demo, theme editor) get fixes only, no new features, until a user asks; no new UI shape pins; no new prose lints.
desiredOutcome: every documented claim a reader acts on matches the code: SECURITY.md names the known open read shapes, the README, QUICKSTART, examples and comments make no false claim, there is one quick-start, the demo shows today's text, and a newcomer and a contributor each have a one-page start

findings.issue: The secret-read rows say a call that names a secret file is refused and name only one gap (a read that never names the file). SECURITY.md names a second class: a read verb the guard's list lacks, with the secret named in plain sight. decide() allows cut, sort, jq, comm, vim and find -exec cat naming .env.production and blocks only listed verbs such as cat and less.
findings.resolution: Say a call naming a secret file beside a read verb the guard lists is refused, and name both open classes, linking SECURITY.md, in all three places.

findings.issue: The first screen says out-of-plan edits are enforced only while a phase runs and observed before that; the code has three tiers (no manifest observes, a manifest with nothing running warns, a running phase denies), and README.md:132, plugins/audit/README.md:572 and QUICKSTART.md:85 each state the gate's timing differently, none naming the warn tier.
findings.resolution: State the three tiers once in the same words wherever the timing is stated, or point each at /audit:doctor, which prints the active tier.

findings.issue: README says QUICKSTART's read-only /audit:doctor step checks the install before anything is written, but QUICKSTART now runs /audit:usage --backfill (which writes the .claude/usage ledger) before doctor.
findings.resolution: Put doctor before the backfill in QUICKSTART, or reword the README sentence.

findings.issue: The Decision record's 'Documentation split by audience' entry limits QUICKSTART to install, one audited task and one report, nothing else; the backfill step was added without amending the record, and line 1079 still says the file opens with the reading order although 'Your first change' now opens it. README.md:138-157 still carries its own backfill 'Start here' block beside the rule that a command list in two places is one list and one lie.
findings.resolution: Amend the decision record entry with the reason QUICKSTART now carries the free first look, update :1079, and reduce README's backfill block to a pointer.

findings.issue: 'Your first change' sends a fresh clone straight to tools/verify.sh, which needs the npm devDependencies (vitest, playwright) and a Playwright Chromium that CI installs with npm ci and npx playwright install; the page names neither, so its one command fails on a fresh clone, and the PR template's verify.sh checkbox inherits the gap.
findings.resolution: Add npm ci and npx playwright install chromium to the page after the clone.

findings.issue: Not every shape SECURITY.md names has a characterization case: comm, cut, sort, jq, an editor and find -exec cat (secret reads) and sort -o and git -C reset --hard (shell writes) have none, and sr25's label is garbled.
findings.resolution: Add known-open rows for those shapes beside watched twins, and reword sr25.

findings.issue: The comment points at SECURITY.md's _command_is_read_only paragraph, but SECURITY.md never names that function.
findings.resolution: Point at the paragraph by its lead sentence.

findings.issue: An ordinal pointer ('Item 6 of Known bypass classes') and two 'the N <noun>' counts in prose, which the author must police.
findings.resolution: Refer to the item by its title and drop both counts.

findings.issue: The rewritten command enumeration leaves out shipped commands, /audit:usage among them, which QUICKSTART sends the reader to.
findings.resolution: Point at the command table instead of enumerating.

findings.issue: The invariant row 'Never read secrets, never log tokens' is graded enforced, contradicting SECURITY.md's name-based secret guard and the open shapes this phase documented.
findings.resolution: Grade it as name-based refusal with the open shapes linked.

findings.issue: The backfill is said to spend no tokens and to write only the .claude/usage ledger; /audit:usage is a model-invoked command that costs an ordinary turn to relay, and in a git repo it also takes and releases a lock under the git common dir.
findings.resolution: Say it runs no agent and no analysis, costs one ordinary turn, and leaves only the self-ignoring ledger in the working tree.

findings.issue: This phase adds a top-level gifs record to the sidecar; branches that re-captured screenshots with the old writer rewrite the file as note and images only, so a merge can conflict or drop the record and turn capture-demo-gif.py --check red; any merged change to the refusal text or the status render also moves the text digest.
findings.resolution: Merge-time reconciliation: after each phase that re-captured screenshots merges, confirm the gifs entry survives and run capture-demo-gif.py --check, re-recording only if the digest moved.

findings.issue: The panel trust-boundary text describes this branch's base (GET / unguarded, pidfile written with plain open and no chmod, reaching the port is reaching the token); the panel phase requires the token on GET / and writes the pidfile owner-only without touching SECURITY.md, so the merge is clean and the paragraph silently stale.
findings.resolution: Merge-time reconciliation with the panel phase: rewrite the paragraph to the token-guarded page and the owner-only pidfile and requote commands/panel.md.

findings.issue: The rewritten end of Known bypass classes item 6 sits next to another phase's edit of item 7 and its fail-mode rows, so a merge may conflict though no sentence becomes false.
findings.resolution: Resolve at merge keeping both edits.

tasks.title: CONTRIBUTING opens with a one-page Your first change
tasks.description: A first external PR today means reading CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING and the UI skills before the first line, and nothing says which of them a given change needs. Add a 'Your first change' section at the top of CONTRIBUTING.md, at most one page, folding in Dev setup rather than repeating it: what to read for a doc fix, a Python fix and a UI fix (the skill table in CLAUDE.md), that PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md is needed only for a new .py, the one command to iterate with (tools/verify.sh --fast) and the one before a PR (tools/verify.sh), what CI checks, and the optional tools (Node for vitest and the browser gates, Pillow for the demo GIF). No duration or count unless it carries the command that re-derives it. Acceptance line: from that page alone, a first-time contributor can tell what to read for their kind of change, which single command to run before a PR and what CI will check, without opening PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md unless they add a .py file.

outcome.technical: CONTRIBUTING.md opens with a one-page 'Your first change' section that folds in the old Dev setup (clone, local marketplace, the guard-edits dev-mode note) instead of repeating it: what to read for a doc fix, a Python fix and a UI fix (pointing at the skill rows in CLAUDE.md), that PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md is needed only for a new .py file, tools/verify.sh --fast to iterate and tools/verify.sh before a PR, and what CI checks. The tools paragraph names what the plain verify.sh run needs beyond the stdlib-only plugin - Node (vitest, ajv-cli, the browser gates), ruff and vermin (pip, pinned in CI) and the Claude Code CLI (claude plugin validate) - and says Pillow is needed only for a manual demo-GIF regeneration, because the --check path never imports it. The old reading-order list stays as 'Reading order beyond this page'. No count or duration without its command; doc_prose_numbers and doc_link_drift are clean.
outcome.descriptive: CONTRIBUTING.md now opens with one page that tells a first-time contributor what to read for their kind of change, the one command to run before a PR, what CI checks and which tools it needs.

intentCheck.basis: audit-reviewer (task mode, two rounds): one medium finding (a false claim that Node and Pillow were the only non-stdlib tools) fixed and re-reviewed clean against verify.sh, ci.yml and capture-demo-gif.py

tasks.title: issue and PR templates point a contributor at the one page
tasks.description: .github holds only workflows, so an issue arrives without the version or the doctor output needed to act on it, and a PR without the checks the repo requires. Add a bug template asking for /audit:version, /audit:doctor output, the command run and what happened; a feature template asking which module and what it blocks, which is where the freeze decision's revisit trigger is observed; a config.yml that routes exploitable weaknesses to SECURITY.md's private address instead of a public issue; and a PR template linking 'Your first change' with tools/verify.sh green and a red-first proof for any new check. gate-only: new Markdown and YAML; selftests runs the prose-number lint, which reads every committed .md.

outcome.technical: Four new files under .github: a bug template asking for /audit:version and /audit:doctor output, the command run and what happened; a feature template asking which module and what it blocks, naming CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Optional modules take fixes only' Decision record entry so a request about an optional module is the evidence its revisit trigger waits for, with a generic line for any other entry; a config.yml routing exploitable weaknesses to SECURITY.md's private reporting section instead of a public issue; and a pull request template linking 'Your first change', with checkboxes for a green tools/verify.sh and a red-first proof of any new check.
outcome.descriptive: Issues and pull requests now arrive with the version, the doctor output and the checks the repository needs, and a request about an optional module is pointed at the decision it can reopen.

intentCheck.basis: audit-reviewer (task mode): one medium finding (name the optional-modules decision entry) fixed as proposed

tasks.title: decision record: optional modules take fixes only, no new UI shape pins, no new prose lints
tasks.description: The surface to maintain grows through discretionary work, so add one Decision record entry with three parts. (a) The panel, the usage views, the ADO connector, the demo and the theme editor take fixes only, no new features, until a user asks; exceptions named up front: the cost-truth work in the usage views (P104), the panel's state-truth fixes (P105) and an ADO feature a real user requests. (b) No new UI shape pins: when a UI part changes, its pins move to vitest or browser behaviour checks, with tools/count-ui-pins.py as the budget. (c) No new lints over prose or repository numbers, stating the consequence: a false documentation claim keeps no mechanical guard and is caught by review at release. Phrase each revisit trigger as an observable property of the system, as the entry on reversed decisions asks (for example, a user report that an optional module blocks their work), never as a count.

outcome.technical: One Decision record entry at the end of CONTRIBUTING.md's Decision record: (a) the panel, the usage views, the ADO connector, the demo and the theme editor take fixes only until a user asks, with the cost-truth work in the usage views, the panel's state-truth fixes and a user-requested ADO feature named as the exceptions; (b) no new UI shape pins, with tools/count-ui-pins.py as the budget and a changed UI part moving its pins to vitest or browser behaviour checks; (c) no new lints over prose or repository numbers, with the consequence that a false documentation claim is caught by review at release. Each part has its own revisit trigger phrased as an observable event, not a count. No plan ids appear in the entry.
outcome.descriptive: CONTRIBUTING.md records that the optional modules take fixes only until a user asks, that UI changes add no new shape pins, and that no new prose or number lints are added, each with a revisit trigger a reader can observe.

intentCheck.basis: audit-reviewer (task mode): one medium finding (private plan ids in the public entry) fixed as proposed

tasks.title: a passed gate row whose changed paths are all undeclared is not a ledger contradiction
tasks.description: The gate recorder and the committed-ledger check disagree about one shape. run-test-gate records a task gate as passed when a path changed during the run that the work under test does not declare (TREE CHANGED OUTSIDE THIS WORK moves the exit code not at all, by design, because a sibling or the orchestrator may write in a shared tree), and it lists that path in observations.treeMutated with a basis saying none of the changed paths is declared. tools/check-example-ledgers.py el1 then reports that committed row as a contradiction ("records 'passed' while its own observations.treeMutated names ..."), so any branch whose committed evidence holds such a row stays red. Seen on this phase's branch on 2026-10-06: the orchestrator closed one task (a journal write) while a sibling task's recorded gate was running in the same worktree; the row was committed with that task and the next gate went red on it. Make the two agree on the recorder's documented rule: a passed row contradicts itself only when a changed path is one the work under test declares. Read the declared set from what the row records (its scope or the basis it carries), never from today's manifest, and if a row records no declared set, say so as its own finding rather than guessing. Decide with the basis in the outcome whether treeMutated is the right field for undeclared changes or whether the recorder should name them apart; a recorder change is out of this task's files, so record it as a follow-up if that is the answer. The committed rows already in the tree must pass the check after the fix.

add: tools/check-example-ledgers.py: a committed row recording passed whose treeMutated names only paths outside the work it declares is accepted, while a passed row naming a declared path is still reported as a contradiction
tools/check-example-ledgers.py: a row that records no declared set is its own finding, never silently accepted or rejected; and the committed ledgers in the tree pass

outcome.technical: tools/check-example-ledgers.py's contradiction rule now follows the recorder's own: a committed row recording passed contradicts itself only when its treeBasis says at least one changed path is declared by the work under test. The declared split is read from the ownership sentence run-test-gate's classify_mutations appends to treeBasis, never from today's manifest. Four branches: no ownership sentence is its own finding ('records no declared set'); 'the work under test declares no files' is a contradiction, because the recorder then attributes every changed path to the gate; 'N of M changed path(s) are declared' with N above zero is a contradiction quoting N of M; and N of zero is accepted. treeMutated stays the field (the evidence module deliberately declines a second owned-paths key); a structured owned count in the row is a possible follow-up so readers need not parse a sentence, and el30 pins the recorder's wording against the constants that parse it. Cases el27-el30, written before the implementation and seen failing (25/29); the stamp-verification red helper cannot prove an inline tools/ suite, because copying the test file over HEAD copies the fix with it. Fixture paths are spelled without a .py suffix so the tool-basename lint does not read them as references.
outcome.descriptive: The committed-ledger check now follows the gate recorder's own rule, so a passed gate whose only changed paths belong to other work no longer turns a branch red, while a rewrite of the work's own files is still caught.

intentCheck.basis: audit-reviewer (task mode): clean; the parsed sentence matches the recorder byte for byte and el30 guards it; the plain check passes over every committed ledger

tasks.title: the documents agree on the secret guard, the gate's tiers and the first-run order
tasks.description: Fixes review findings P103-R1 to P103-R5 and P103-R8 to P103-R11, which share files. (1) Every secret-read claim (plugins/audit/README.md's guard rows and invariant row, README.md) says a call naming a secret file beside a read verb the guard lists is refused, and names both open classes - a read that never names the file, and an unlisted verb naming it - linking SECURITY.md; the invariant row is graded as name-based refusal. (2) Wherever a document states when the plan gate enforces (README.md's first screen and later section, plugins/audit/README.md, QUICKSTART.md) it states the three tiers in the same words - observe with no plan, warn with a plan and nothing running, deny while a phase runs - or points at /audit:doctor, which prints the active tier. (3) QUICKSTART runs the read-only /audit:doctor check before the free backfill, so README's sentence that doctor checks the install before anything is written holds; README's own backfill block becomes a pointer to QUICKSTART. (4) The backfill is described as running no agent and no analysis, costing one ordinary turn, and leaving only the self-ignoring ledger in the working tree. (5) CONTRIBUTING.md's Decision record entry on documentation by audience is amended with the reason QUICKSTART now carries the free first look at spend, and its line about how the file opens names 'Your first change'; 'Your first change' adds npm ci and npx playwright install chromium after the clone, and the PR template's verify.sh line says the same. (6) An ordinal pointer in SECURITY.md and two counts in CONTRIBUTING.md's prose are replaced by names. (7) plugins/audit/README.md's command enumeration becomes a pointer to the command table. (8) commands/usage.md's brief no longer tells the agent both to fence and not to fence the output.
